subject: Request: split-keystore escrow + rotation evidence for BYOK integration
messages:
From: security@cloudwave.com (CloudWave Security)
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Request: split-keystore escrow + rotation evidence for BYOK integration

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call earlier. As part of CloudWave's BYOK acceptance checklist we need a compact evidence package covering:

- Proof of split-keystore / escrow procedures for customer-supplied keys (what artifacts you hold, what you DON’T hold).
- HSM vendor attestation and certificate for the cluster that handles tenant-wrapping operations.
- Rotation logs for the last 12 months (redacted to remove tenant identifiers is fine).
- Confirmation of in-transit encryption ciphers and key derivation methods used during the handshake.
- Retention policy for key-related telemetry and access logs.

Can you confirm what you can provide by next Wednesday (24 Aug)? If possible please include a sample redaction and the minimum set of fields we should expect in the rotation manifest.

We may need a brief statement for our procurement team about whether Redwood ever has the ability to reconstruct raw customer key material.

Thanks,
Sam Reyes
CloudWave Security
security@cloudwave.com
Attachment: request_checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com (Kimberly Park)
To: security@cloudwave.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: split-keystore escrow + rotation evidence for BYOK integration

Sam —

Appreciate the clear list. We can assemble a focused evidence bundle that addresses each bullet. High-level summary of what we'll provide:

1) Split-keystore ledger (redacted CSV) showing key ID hashes, ceremony step timestamps, escrow-recipients (pseudonymized), and retention markers.
2) HSM attestation from our vendor (Thales) including FIPS/Cert chain (PDF).
3) KMS rotation manifest (CSV) with rotation_timestamp, rotation_reason, performing_principal (role only), and redacted key_fingerprint.
4) Sample key-handshake log (redacted) and short note on the handshake KDF + wrapping cipher suite.
5) Short statement confirming Redwood never stores raw customer key material and an explanation of our split-escrow process.
6) Soc2 snapshot evidencing the control IDs that map to key management (we'll include the relevant page).

We will not provide full tenant identifiers in the ledger; we will replace tenant IDs with stable hashes and include a mapping column only if you sign the attached redlined NDA (we will share the redline).

Target: send packaged artifacts + brief cover note by Tue 24 Aug EOD. If procurement needs a separate compliance attestation, let us know and we'll include an authorized signature from our security team.

Thanks — Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_evidence_plan.txt (plain text)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com (Jonas Weber)
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, security@cloudwave.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2027 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: split-keystore escrow + rotation evidence for BYOK integration

Adding technical detail so CloudWave has clarity on redaction approach and provenance: 

- Split-keystore: We maintain a two-party split where Redwood holds a wrapping key in an HSM (Key-Wrap Key) and the escrowed shares are stored encrypted across two geographically separated vault clusters. We never hold the full unwrapped customer key. The ledger contains: ceremony_step, timestamp_utc, operation_id (uuid), key_fingerprint_sha256, escrow_share_ids (pseudonymized), operator_role.

- HSM: Current vendor is Thales Luna Network HSM. Attestation includes the HSM serial, firmware hash, and vendor-signed certificate. The HSM performs wrapping operations under FIPS-compliant key usage policies.

- Rotation exports: We'll give a CSV with headers: rotation_timestamp_utc, key_alias_hash, rotation_type (scheduled|compromise), performed_by_role, previous_kid_hash, new_kid_hash. We will redact tenant-specific aliases by hashing with a Pepper value stored in our secrets manager (we'll include the hashing salt fingerprint in the manifest so CloudWave can verify consistency).

- TLS / In-transit: We use TLS1.3 with AES-GCM or CHACHA20-POLY1305 (server preference) for control plane and mTLS for private deployments. Handshake KDF: HKDF-SHA256 with AES-KW for envelope wrapping on internal flows.

- Logs: Access to key material is audited via an immutable append-only log stored in the telemetry cluster. We'll produce an exported slice covering the last 12 months for the keys you reference.

I'll prepare the redacted CSV and a short runbook describing the redaction script and the verification steps (sha256 checksums).

Jonas
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: kms_redaction_runbook.md (markdown)

From: irene_choi@redwood.com (Irene Choi)
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, security@cloudwave.com
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: split-keystore escrow + rotation evidence for BYOK integration

Kim / Jonas —

This looks good. A couple of asks before we hand over any artifacts:

- Please append a short attestation paragraph (signed by Redwood Security) stating: 
  * Redwood does not possess raw customer key material for BYOK tenants.
  * Escrowed shares are encrypted with customer-derived material and our operator roles lack reconstruction capability.

- Include the cipher-suite list for the public control plane and the private VPC connectors (I prefer a one-line canonical list).

- For the ledger CSV include a column "redaction_proof_sha256" that maps to the redaction script output so CloudWave can reproduce the same redactions locally if they choose.

I drafted a redlined NDA that allows us to share tenant-hashed ledgers under constrained conditions; attaching it for Kim to send.

Irene
Director, Product Security
Attachment: redlined-data-sharing-nda.pdf (pdf)

From: procurement@cloudwave.com (CloudWave Procurement)
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: security@cloudwave.com, alice.hughes@gravity-ps.com
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 09:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: split-keystore escrow + rotation evidence for BYOK integration

Kim —

Procurement here. Thanks for coordinating. A couple of follow-ups so we can approve the technical review: 

1) We need a one-paragraph statement for our legal file that explicitly says whether Redwood could reconstruct raw customer keys under any normal or emergency workflow.
2) Can you confirm retention windows for key-access logs and the SLA for producing ad-hoc audit slices?
3) Please include the relevant SOC2 control IDs or mapping table for key management.

If you can send those items along with your evidence bundle that should be sufficient for our vendor risk board.

Best,
Rhea Kaplan
CloudWave Procurement
Attachment: purchase_order_template.docx (docx)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com (Kimberly Park)
To: security@cloudwave.com, procurement@cloudwave.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: split-keystore escrow + rotation evidence for BYOK integration

Team —

Attached is the evidence bundle for CloudWave: split_keystore_ledger_redacted.csv, hsm_attestation_thales_202706.pdf, kms_rotation_manifest.csv, key_handshake_log_sample.txt, encryption_in_transit_cipherlist.txt, redlined-data-sharing-nda.pdf, and the redwood-soc2-snapshot.pdf.

Quick answers in-line for procurement:

- Reconstruction: Redwood cannot reconstruct raw customer key material for BYOK tenants. Our documented emergency workflow requires an escrow reconstruction that must be authorized by a multi-party ceremony including customer authorization; Redwood operators lack the unencrypted shares required to recreate raw keys. (Formal attestation included in the bundle.)
- Retention: Key-access audit logs are retained for 18 months by default; rotation manifests are retained for 36 months. Ad-hoc audit slices can be produced within 5 business days, subject to NDA terms and redaction scope.
- SOC2 mapping: See redwood-soc2-snapshot.pdf page 4 for control IDs CC6/CM-2/CM-4 equivalent mappings for key lifecycle and access auditing.

Drive link to the evidence bundle (read-only): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AbCdefGH
DocuSign link for NDA if CloudWave agrees to the redline: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC123456
HubSpot ticket: HS-987654

If you want a short 30-minute walkthrough of the artifacts, Jonas and I can do a call Thu 26 Aug.

Thanks,
Kim
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
